title: Paired evaluation of LLM-alone, LLM+deterministic-validator, and LLM+validator+deterministic-gate pipelines for intent-to-configuration NetOps changes (repaired)
research_question: Compared to LLM-alone generation, does coupling an LLM with a domain-specific deterministic verifier and a deterministic gate (automated accept/reject policy) reduce unsafe network-change proposals (reachability/policy violations) on a paired intent-to-configuration task suite?
confirmatory_hypotheses: H1: The LLM+validator pipeline produces fewer unsafe configurations (any reachability or policy violation) than LLM-alone on identical intents (paired test).
H2: Replacing a human-in-the-loop gate with a deterministic automated gate (strict accept/reject with bounded automated repairs) further reduces unsafe proposals relative to LLM+validator alone.

H3: Differences in unsafe-output rates between pipeline pairs (A vs B, B vs C) are detectable using the registered paired binary analysis (paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline) with the preregistered sample.
exploratory_questions: E1: How do latency tradeoffs (end-to-end generation+validation+repair time) vary by pipeline and intent complexity?
E2: What fraction of unsafe proposals are repaired successfully by a single automated repair attempt?
E3: How sensitive are primary results to baseline unsafe-rate assumptions (25%–35%)?
benchmark_scope: Public and synthetic intent-to-configuration tasks (routing, ACL, BGP-policy) derived from public topology/config sources and synthesized variants.
Sandboxed emulation using deterministic Batfish-style checks (reachability, ACL policy, BGP consistency) on canonical topologies included with this study.
model_scope: Hosted public LLM (generation and repair) via hosted model API (model_id: gpt-4o-mini).
Deterministic verifier running in docker (Batfish v2023.10 image).
transformation_scope: Canonicalization: whitespace/ordering normalization, canonical interface naming, stable ASN rewriting rules.
Semantic-preserving normalization of ACL entries to canonical AST form used by verifier.
primary_estimand: Paired absolute difference in unsafe-proposal rate (proportion of intents producing any reachability or policy violation) between LLM-alone (baseline) and LLM+validator (condition B); and between LLM+validator and LLM+validator+deterministic-gate (condition C). Estimand name: paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline.
secondary_estimands: Absolute and relative risk reduction (with 95% Wilson CIs) in unsafe proposals for A vs B and B vs C.
Paired difference in median end-to-end latency (ms) between pipeline pairs.
Proportion of intents for which automated repair succeeded (per-condition).
sampling_plan: 200 paired intents total, stratified by complexity: low=80, medium=80, high=40. Inclusion: intents express a single network-change goal (routing, ACL, or BGP policy) and map to <=5 devices in a canonical topology. Exclusion: intents requiring proprietary vendor features not supported by verifier, intents lacking a deterministic mapping to configs. Each intent yields three paired proposals (A: LLM-alone, B: LLM+validator+1 auto-repair attempt, C: LLM+validator+deterministic-gate with up to 2 auto-repair attempts). Random seed for intent sampling/synthetic mutator: 42.
analysis_plan: Confirmatory analysis uses the registered analysis executor 'paired_binary_analysis_v1' (estimand: paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline). Primary test: paired binary comparison (McNemar-equivalent via executor) between A vs B and B vs C on binary unsafe flag (any reachability/policy violation). Report absolute and relative reductions with 95% CIs and exact p-values. Latency comparisons: paired Wilcoxon signed-rank test (reported descriptively) if non-normal. Pre-specified subgroup analyses by intent complexity (low/med/high) are exploratory and multiplicity-corrected (Benjamini–Hochberg) for false-discovery control. All tests two-sided, alpha=0.05. Failed-call treatment: follow contract-compatible options ['complete_pair_primary','complete_pair_primary_with_failure_as_zero_sensitivity'] as implemented by the executor.
multiplicity_plan: Primary confirmatory family: two paired comparisons (A vs B, B vs C). Alpha allocation: nominal alpha=0.05 applied separately to each confirmatory pair (both treated as primary co-primary comparisons). Exploratory subgroup tests use Benjamini–Hochberg correction across reported exploratory p-values.
missingness_plan: If a pipeline condition fails on an intent due to provider/infrastructure error, the pair is handled per the analysis contract failed_call_treatment: (1) attempt deterministic re-execution once per preregistered retry policy; (2) if still failing, follow 'complete_pair_primary' (drop entire intent-pair from primary analysis) and report sensitivity using 'complete_pair_primary_with_failure_as_zero_sensitivity' (treat missing condition as unsafe) in supplementary results. All failures, retries, and hashes logged.

benchmark_names: canonical topology pack (public router topologies + synthetic variants)
risk_factors: Poisoned or adversarial retrieval/context not applicable (no retrieval-augmented generation used).
Maliciously crafted synthetic intents producing out-of-scope configs.
Verifier-rule gaps leading to missed violations (construct-validity contamination).
detection_procedures: Provenance checks on all synthetic-intent generator runs (seed 42) and checksums for canonical artifacts.
Deterministic signature-based filtering for intents outside allowed scope (reject if AST size or vendor-feature token out-of-scope).
Unit tests for verifier coverage that assert detection of seeded violation templates (reachability, ACL bypass, BGP-export mismatch).
item_flagging_rules: Flag and exclude any intent whose generated config (baseline or repaired) uses vendor features outside verified feature-list.
Flag intents whose verifier unit-tests fail on seeded known-violation cases for the topology class.
contamination_plan.analysis_treatment: Flagged items excluded from primary confirmatory analysis; exclusions and counts reported. Sensitivity analyses include excluded items treated as unsafe. All detector/flagging logic deterministic and preregistered.
residual_uncertainty: Verifier coverage may not capture every real-world invariant (residual construct-validity uncertainty).
Automated deterministic gate simulates operator gate but is not equivalent to real-world contextual HITL behavior.

budget_scenarios.description: Expected-case budget assuming baseline unsafe-rate 30%, automated repair success profile: first repair succeeds 50% of unsafe cases, second repair succeeds remaining 50% of unsafe cases (on average 1.5 repairs per unsafe intent).
transformations: repair-prompting (one or two additional generation calls as needed)
budget_scenarios.feasibility_rationale: Total expected model calls = sum over pipelines: A=200*1=200; B=200*(1 + 0.30*1)=260; C=200*(1 + 0.30*1.5)=290; overall=200+260+290=750. 750 < capability manifest max_planned_model_calls (10000). Docker-based verifier and CPU execution suffice for deterministic checks.

budget_scenarios.description: Conservative worst-case where every intent requires the maximum allowed repairs in B (1) and C (2).
budget_scenarios.feasibility_rationale: Worst-case model calls: A=200; B=200*(1+1)=400; C=200*(1+2)=600; total=200+400+600=1200. 1200 < 10000 allowed calls and is executable within 7 wall-clock days given hosted model API and docker verifier.

power_plan.target_effect: Absolute reduction of 10 percentage points in unsafe-proposal rate (e.g., from baseline 30% to 20%)
power_plan.calculation_method: McNemar-style paired binary analysis approximation implemented by 'paired_binary_analysis_v1' executor. Power statements based on baseline unsafe-rate assumptions and assumed discordant-pair structure.
assumptions: Baseline unsafe-proposal rate ~ 30% (literature-motivated conservative central estimate).
Discordant-pair structure consistent with 10pp absolute reduction mapping to expected discordant proportion enabling detection at n=200.
Two-sided alpha=0.05 for each co-primary paired comparison.
power_plan.minimum_detectable_effect_notes: With n=200 paired intents and baseline 30% unsafe rate, we estimate >80% power to detect ~10pp absolute reduction under plausible discordant-pair assumptions used by the paired_binary_analysis_v1 executor. Sensitivity analyses will report power under baseline rates 25% and 35%; expected power range approximately 72%–86% depending on discordant composition.
sensitivity_analyses: Recompute primary p-values under assumed baseline unsafe rates 25% and 35%.
Report results treating failed/excluded pairs as unsafe (conservative sensitivity).

semantic_equivalence_checks: Automated AST diffs: a transformation is accepted if semantic AST equivalence holds for reachability-irrelevant reorderings.
End-to-end simulation check: transformed baseline config must produce identical reachability matrix on verifier for verified topologies (unit tests).
automatic_rejection_rules: Reject transformation if AST-level semantic-preserving predicates fail (e.g., reordering changes permit new reachability).
Reject if canonicalization introduces vendor-feature tokens outside verified feature-list.
transformation_validation.audit_sample_policy: Random 10% sample of transformed configs (seed 42) undergo full end-to-end verification and are included in public CI artifacts alongside unit-test hashes.
transformation_validation.mapping_validation: Unit tests (dockerized) assert that seeded config variants map to expected canonical ASTs and that verifier assertions (reachability/policy checks) produce expected outcomes.
residual_risks: Edge cases in canonicalization (vendor-specific semantics) may not be fully captured by automated checks.
Semantic-equivalence heuristics may miss subtle operational semantics not represented in verifier models.

remaining_noncritical_uncertainties: R1: Verifier coverage is bounded to the declared rule set and canonical topologies; real-world production topologies may include invariants outside the verifier scope (external-validity limit).
R2: The deterministic automated gate simulates a constrained HITL behavior but does not capture human contextual judgments (behavioral-generalization limit).
R3: Power estimates depend on baseline unsafe-rate and discordant-pair structure; results include sensitivity analyses but exact power may vary in other populations.
